mainTopic: Marriages of a חרש and חרשת: תרומה, כתובה, and אשם תלוי
overview: The amud opens with the last words of an earlier answer: men would avoid marrying a חרשת if she could do מיאון forever. The גמרא then compares a קטנה and a חרשת, whose marriages are both only מדרבנן. A קטנה married to a כהן eats תרומה, but a חרשת does not. This is explained through a chain of גזירות: a חרש might feed a פקחת wife, and from תרומה דרבנן he could slide into תרומה דאורייתא. Next, a קטנה has a כתובה but a חרשת does not, so that men will not avoid marrying her. The גמרא brings a משנה and a ברייתא as sources. A פקחת married to a חרש also gets no כתובה, because women want to marry even more than men do. רבא praises רב מלכיו for giving a חרש's wife a כתובה from the חרש's own property, since a wife helps him even more than a maidservant. Then שמואל rules about an אשם תלוי for relations with a חרש's wife, in two versions. Both versions are built on רבי אלעזר's view that a חרש's acts are a ספק. The amud ends with רב אשי asking for רבי אלעזר's reason, and his question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: People would avoid marrying her
steps.stepSummary: The tail end of an earlier answer: if a חרשת could do מיאון, men would avoid marrying her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Men would hold back and not marry her.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the closing words of the previous discussion. The גמרא is finishing its explanation of why the חכמים did not give a חרשת the option of מיאון: men would be afraid to marry her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קטנה's option to refuse ends when she grows up. A חרשת never 'grows out' of her condition, so her option to refuse would never end. That open-ended risk would make men hesitant to marry her, so the חכמים did not give her מיאון.

keyTerms.meaning: they hold back, avoid
they marry (take a wife)
a girl's refusal that ends a marriage made for her מדרבנן while she was a minor

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים did not give a חרשת the option of מיאון, so that men would not be scared off from marrying her.

phrases.english: They would hold back and not marry her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier discussion about מיאון for a חרשת, which began before this section.
steps.terutzMaskana: No מיאון for a חרשת, because men would avoid marrying her.

steps.title: Why can a minor eat תרומה but a deaf-mute woman cannot?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a קטנה married to a כהן eats תרומה while a חרשת does not. It brings the testimony of רבי יוחנן בן גודגדא as its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between a minor girl, who eats תרומה, and a deaf-mute woman, who does not? We learned in a משנה that רבי יוחנן בן גודגדא testified about two cases. A deaf-mute woman married off by her father can be divorced with a גט. A minor Israelite girl married to a כהן eats תרומה. That implies a deaf-mute woman does not eat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. It points out that two cases which seem alike get different rulings, and it proves this from a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both a קטנה and a חרשת can only be married מדרבנן, because neither has full legal ability to marry. Yet רבי יוחנן בן גודגדא testified that the קטנה eats תרומה. He said this only about the קטנה, which implies the חרשת does not eat. So why treat them differently?

keyTerms.meaning: a minor girl
a deaf-mute woman, treated as legally not competent
the holy portion of produce, eaten only by כהנים and their households
testified (a formal testimony about a tradition)
whereas, but by contrast

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה never says outright that a חרשת may not eat תרומה. The גמרא reads that from the fact that the testimony about eating mentions only the קטנה.

phrases.english: And what is different about a minor girl
that she eats תרומה,
and what is different about a deaf-mute woman
that she does not eat תרומה?

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: הֵעִיד רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן גּוּדְגְּדָא
phrases.english: As we learned: Rabbi Yochanan ben Gudgada testified
about a deaf-mute woman whose father married her off
that she leaves the marriage with a גט,
and about a minor girl, daughter of an Israelite,
who married a כהן
that she eats תרומה,
whereas a deaf-mute woman does not eat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the מיאון discussion ends.
steps.kashyaTarget: The different rulings for a קטנה and a חרשת regarding תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both marriages are only מדרבנן. So if one wife eats תרומה, the other should too.

steps.title: A decree: a deaf-mute husband might feed a deaf-mute wife
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים forbade a חרשת from eating, out of concern that a חרש כהן married to a חרשת would also feed her.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree, out of concern that a deaf-mute man will feed a deaf-mute woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first answer. The rule against the חרשת eating is a protective גזירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture a חרשת married to a healthy כהן, and suppose she were allowed to eat. People might then let a חרש כהן feed his חרשת wife too. That marriage is weaker, so to block it the חכמים forbade every חרשת.

keyTerms.meaning: a protective decree of the חכמים
lest, out of concern that
he will feed
a deaf-mute man

phrases.english: It is a decree, lest a deaf-mute man feed a deaf-mute woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.terutzMaskana: A חרשת does not eat, because of the case of a חרש feeding a חרשת.

steps.title: So what? She is like a minor eating forbidden food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. Even in that case, the one eating is like a קטן eating נבלות, and nobody is required to stop that.
steps.simpleTranslation: So let him feed her! She is like a minor who eats נבלות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the first answer. It argues that the case the decree was worried about is not really a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חרשת is not legally competent, so she has the status of a קטן. When a קטן eats something forbidden, like נבלות, בית דין does not have to stop him. So there is no reason to make a decree just to prevent a חרש from feeding a חרשת.

keyTerms.meaning: so let him/her eat
a minor
meat of animals not properly slaughtered

phrases.english: So let him feed her,
it is like a minor eating נבלות!
phrases.notes: A well-known rule: if a minor eats forbidden food, בית דין doesn't have to step in to stop him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The decree about a חרש feeding a חרשת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The feared result is harmless in law, because nobody must stop someone who has a minor's status from eating forbidden food.

steps.title: A decree: a deaf-mute husband might feed a competent wife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the reason. The real concern is a חרש כהן feeding a פקחת wife, who is competent and must be stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is a decree, out of concern that a deaf-mute man will feed a competent woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא replaces its first answer with a better one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the worry is about a healthy woman (פקחת) married to a חרש. Her marriage is only מדרבנן, so on a Torah level she is not a כהן's wife and may not eat תרומה. Unlike a חרשת, she is fully responsible for what she eats, so the concern is real.

keyTerms.meaning: a legally competent woman (not deaf-mute)

phrases.english: It is a decree, lest a deaf-mute man feed a competent woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4 by switching to a different feared case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The decree guarded against a חרש feeding a חרשת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The decree guards against a חרש feeding a פקחת, who must be kept from forbidden food.

steps.title: Let her at least eat rabbinic תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again. Since the פקחת's marriage is מדרבנן, she should be allowed to eat at least תרומה דרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A deaf-mute man with a competent woman too: let her eat תרומה that is only rabbinic!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second answer. It argues that even the חרש with a פקחת could be allowed partly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some תרומה is only required מדרבנן. A marriage that works מדרבנן should be enough for תרומה that is itself only מדרבנן. So why forbid her completely?

keyTerms.meaning: also, too
תרומה required only by the חכמים, not by the Torah

phrases.english: And a deaf-mute man with a competent woman too,
let her eat תרומה that is rabbinic!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחֵרֵשׁ בְּפִקַּחַת נָמֵי לֵיכוֹל בִּתְרוּמָה דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The full ban on a פקחת married to a חרש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rabbinic marriage should be enough for rabbinic תרומה.

steps.title: He might end up feeding her Torah-level תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים forbade even תרומה דרבנן, out of concern that he would go on to feed her תרומה דאורייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree, because perhaps he will come to feed her תרומה that is from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the last challenge, and this closes the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she were allowed rabbinic תרומה, people would not keep track of which kind she was eating. She could end up eating Torah-level תרומה, which is truly forbidden to her. So the חכמים banned all תרומה for her, and that is why every חרשת is kept from eating as well.

keyTerms.meaning: perhaps, maybe
he will come to (end up doing)
תרומה required by Torah law

steps.whatToRemember: A קטנה married to a כהן eats תרומה, but a חרשת does not. This is a chain of protective decrees: a חרש might feed a פקחת wife, and from rabbinic תרומה he could slide into Torah תרומה.

phrases.english: It is a decree, perhaps he will come
to feed her תרומה that is from the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּזֵירָה דִּלְמָא אָתֵי לְאוֹכֹלַהּ בִּתְרוּמָה דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Protective decree on top of a protective decree
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A rabbinic marriage could allow rabbinic תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even rabbinic תרומה is forbidden, so that he does not end up feeding her Torah תרומה.

steps.title: Why does a minor get a marriage contract but a deaf-mute woman does not?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a קטנה has a כתובה while a חרשת does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the difference between a minor girl, who has a marriage contract, and a deaf-mute woman, who does not have a marriage contract?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. Both women are married only מדרבנן, so why does one get a כתובה and the other doesn't?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the discussion was about eating תרומה. Now the גמרא turns to the כתובה. Since neither marriage is fully valid מדאורייתא, we would expect both women to be treated the same.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference? (asking why two similar cases are treated differently)
A girl under the age of adulthood
A deaf-mute woman, treated in halacha as not fully competent
Marriage contract, which promises the wife money if she is divorced or widowed

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאי שְׁנָא קְטַנָּה דְּאִית לַהּ כְּתוּבָּה,
phrases.english: And what is different about a minor girl, that she has a marriage contract,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאי שְׁנָא חֵרֶשֶׁת דְּלֵית לַהּ כְּתוּבָּה?
phrases.english: and what is different about a deaf-mute woman, that she does not have a marriage contract?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא קְטַנָּה דְּאִית לַהּ כְּתוּבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the תרומה discussion to a parallel question about the כתובה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for treating a קטנה and a חרשת differently regarding a כתובה

steps.title: Men would refuse to marry her
steps.stepSummary: If a חרשת received a כתובה, men would avoid marrying her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because if so, men would hold back and not marry her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the חכמים did not give a חרשת a כתובה so that men would still be willing to marry her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is a practical one that protects the חרשת herself. A husband already takes on a hard situation by marrying her, and a required כתובה would push men away completely. Without the obligation, she is more likely to find a husband.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if the opposite rule were true)
They would hold back
They marry

phrases.english: Because if so,
they would hold back and not marry her.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִם כֵּן מִימַּנְעִי וְלָא נָסְבִי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A חרשת gets no required כתובה so that men will not avoid marrying her

steps.title: What is the source that a minor gets a marriage contract?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source showing that a קטנה has a כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a minor girl, from where do we know that she has a marriage contract?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to check the first assumption behind the question: where do we learn that a קטנה gets a כתובה? This sets up the next step, which brings a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question in step 8 rested on two claims. The גמרא will now prove each one, starting with the קטנה.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this? (a request for a source)

phrases.english: And a minor girl, from where do we know that she has a marriage contract?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a source for the first claim in step 8
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that a קטנה is entitled to a כתובה

steps.title: A משנה shows that a minor who is divorced has a marriage contract
steps.stepSummary: A משנה lists women with no כתובה. By implication, a woman divorced with a גט, including a קטנה, does have one.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: A girl who refuses her husband, a woman who is a rabbinically forbidden relative, and a woman who cannot bear children have no marriage contract. The גמרא infers: but a woman who leaves with a bill of divorce, including a minor girl, has a marriage contract.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה that lists women who get no כתובה. From that list it infers that a woman who leaves with a גט, including a קטנה, does get one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה excludes only a קטנה who leaves by refusing her husband. The גמרא reasons that if he instead divorces her with a גט, she is not on the excluded list, so she has a כתובה. This proves that a קטנה's marriage carries a כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה
A minor who refuses her husband and so ends the marriage without a גט
A woman forbidden to her husband as a relative only by rabbinic law
A woman physically unable to bear children
Bill of divorce

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה: A girl who refuses,
and a secondary forbidden relative, and a woman who cannot bear children,
have no marriage contract.
But one who leaves with a bill of divorce, and a minor girl,
phrases.notes: This is the גמרא's own conclusion from the list: a minor divorced with a גט isn't on it, unlike the girl who refuses.

phrases.english: has a marriage contract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source requested in step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From the משנה's list, which excludes only a refusing minor, the גמרא infers that a קטנה divorced with a גט has a כתובה

steps.title: What is the source that a deaf-mute woman has no marriage contract?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source showing that a חרשת has no כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a deaf-mute woman, from where do we know that she has no marriage contract?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא asks for proof of the second claim, that a חרשת does not get a כתובה. This sets up the ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 proved the קטנה half. This step goes after the חרשת half, so that both sides of the question in step 8 are supported.

keyTerms.meaning: She has / she does not have

phrases.english: And a deaf-mute woman, from where do we know that she has no marriage contract?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 10, now for the חרשת
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that a חרשת has no required כתובה

steps.title: A ברייתא about deaf-mute and imbecile marriages
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules on a חרש or שוטה husband and on a פקח husband of a חרשת. If a פקח husband wrote her a כתובה, it is valid because he chose to take on the loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: If a deaf-mute or an imbecile married competent women, even if the deaf-mute later becomes competent and the imbecile becomes sane, the wives have no claim against them. If the husbands want to keep them, the wives have a marriage contract. And a competent man who married a deaf-mute or an imbecile woman, even if he wrote her a hundred maneh, her marriage contract stands, because he chose to lose his own property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. The key line for our question is about a פקח who married a חרשת: a כתובה he wrote her is binding only because he wanted to give it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first case explains that a כתובה written by a חרש or שוטה husband counts for nothing, unless he keeps her after he becomes competent. The second case says a פקח's כתובה to a חרשת is valid, and gives the reason that he chose to lose his own money. That reason hints that he was never required to write it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is taught in a ברייתא
A mentally incompetent person
A fully competent person
To keep them as wives
A coin worth one hundred זוז
To cause a loss to his own property

phrases.english: As it is taught: A deaf-mute and an imbecile who married competent women,
even though the deaf-mute became competent,
and the imbecile became sane,
they have no claim at all against them.
phrases.notes: The wives cannot collect anything, even from a כתובה the husband wrote while he was not competent.

phrases.english: If they want to keep them, they have a marriage contract.
And a competent man who married a deaf-mute or an imbecile woman,
even if he wrote her a hundred maneh,
her marriage contract stands,
because he wanted to cause a loss to his property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא that answers step 12
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A פקח's כתובה to a חרשת is valid only because he chose to write it

steps.title: If he did not choose to write one, she gets nothing
steps.stepSummary: From the reason "because he wanted," the גמרא learns that without his choice a חרשת has no כתובה, so that men will not refuse to marry her.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is that he wanted to. But if he did not want to, she has none, because if so, men would hold back and not marry her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads a lesson out of the ברייתא's wording. The כתובה is valid only because he chose it, so without his choice she has none. This finishes the proof and ties back to the reason given in step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying "because he wanted" means the כתובה is a voluntary gift, not something he owes her. That proves a חרשת has no required כתובה. The reason is the same one from step 9: otherwise men would not marry her.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason is...
But then (it follows that...)
He wanted

steps.whatToRemember: A קטנה has a required כתובה (from the משנה). A חרשת has a כתובה only if her husband chose to write one (from the ברייתא). The חכמים made it this way so that men would not avoid marrying a חרשת.

phrases.english: The reason is that he wanted to,
but if he did not want to, she has none,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִם כֵּן מִימַּנְעִי וְלָא נָסְבִי לַהּ.
phrases.english: because if so, they would hold back and not marry her.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּרָצָה הָא לֹא רָצָה אֵין לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the needed lesson from the ברייתא in step 13 and connects it to step 9
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A חרשת has no required כתובה, only one her husband chooses to write, so that men will still marry her

steps.title: Why not give a כתובה to a woman who marries a deaf man?
steps.stepSummary: Using the same reasoning as before, the גמרא asks why the רבנן didn't set up a כתובה for a פקחת married to a חרש, so women won't avoid marrying deaf men.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a hearing woman who marries a deaf man should also get a כתובה from the רבנן. Otherwise women will hold back and not marry deaf men!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the reason just given for a חרשת and turns it into a challenge for the opposite case: a פקחת married to a חרש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 said a חרשת gets no כתובה so that men won't avoid marrying her. By that same logic, a hearing woman married to a deaf man should get a כתובה. Otherwise women would refuse deaf men. So why didn't the רבנן set this up?

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if that is your reasoning
A woman who can hear and speak (halachically competent)
A deaf-mute man
Let them enact (a rabbinic תקנה)
They will hold back

phrases.english: If so,
a competent woman married to a deaf-mute
let them enact a marriage contract for her,
for otherwise women will hold back and not get married!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the reasoning of step 14 to the reverse case and finds a problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reasoning that a כתובה is set up so people won't avoid marrying someone
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that reasoning is valid, it should also require a כתובה for a פקחת married to a חרש. Yet the רבנן did not set one up.

steps.title: Women want to marry even more than men do
steps.stepSummary: Women want to get married more than men do, so they won't refuse deaf men even without a כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: More than a man wants to marry, a woman wants to be married.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The two cases are not the same, because women are more eager to marry than men.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Men might skip a חרשת if they had to give her a כתובה, so the רבנן spared them that cost. Women, however, will marry a חרש anyway, even with no כתובה. So no תקנה was needed to protect deaf men.

keyTerms.meaning: More than
To marry (said of the man)
To be married (said of the woman)

phrases.english: More than the man wants to marry,
a woman wants to be married.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the two cases using a fact about human nature
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The logic of 'so they won't hold back' should apply equally to men and women.
steps.terutzMaskana: Women are more eager to marry, so they won't hold back. No כתובה is needed for a פקחת married to a חרש.
steps.whatToRemember: A חרשת gets no כתובה so men won't avoid her. A פקחת married to a חרש also gets none, because women won't avoid marrying anyway.

steps.title: רב מלכיו marries off a deaf neighbor with a כתובה
steps.stepSummary: A story: רב מלכיו married his deaf neighbor to a woman and wrote her a כתובה of 400 זוזים from the חרש's own property.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a deaf man who lived in רב מלכיו's neighborhood. רב מלכיו married him to a woman and wrote her a כתובה of four hundred זוזים from the deaf man's property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story where a כתובה was given to a woman married to a חרש. That is the very case where we just learned there is no תקנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חרש could not take on a כתובה himself, and no rabbinic תקנה gave her one. Even so, רב מלכיו wrote one for her from the חרש's assets. The next step explains why he was allowed to do this.

keyTerms.meaning: His neighborhood
He married him off
זוזים, silver coins
His property

phrases.english: There was a certain deaf-mute
who was in the neighborhood of Rav Malkiyyu.
He married him to a woman
and wrote her four hundred zuz
from his property.
phrases.notes: 'His' means the deaf man's property, not רב מלכיו's own money.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא חֵרֵשׁ דַּהֲוָה בְּשִׁבָבוּתֵיהּ דְּרַב מַלְכִּיּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows a practical case where a woman married to a חרש did receive a כתובה, despite the rule in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman married to a חרש was given a כתובה of 400 זוזים from the חרש's property.

steps.title: רבא praises רב מלכיו's wisdom
steps.stepSummary: רבא praises רב מלכיו. We would buy a חרש a maidservant from his money, so surely we may spend it on a wife, who gives two benefits.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Who is as wise as רב מלכיו? He is a great man. He reasoned: if the deaf man wanted a maidservant to serve him, wouldn't we buy one for him? All the more so here, where there are two benefits.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains why רב מלכיו was allowed to take the חרש's money for a כתובה. He uses a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We may use a חרש's money for his needs, like buying a שפחה to serve him. A wife serves him and is also a wife to him, so she gives two benefits. Spending his money on her כתובה is even more justified.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is as wise
He reasoned
A maidservant
We buy
All the more so (a קל וחומר)
Two (benefits)

phrases.english: Rava said:
Who is as wise as Rav Malkiyyu,
for he is a great man.
He reasoned:
If he wanted a maidservant to serve him,
would we not buy one for him?
All the more so here,
where there are two.
phrases.notes: Two benefits: she serves him like a maidservant, and she is also his wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מַאן חַכִּים כְּרַב מַלְכִּיּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and approves the action described in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We may use a חרש's property to give his wife a כתובה, just as we would use it to buy him a שפחה.
steps.whyThisMatters: Even with no תקנה of a כתובה, a בית דין can still provide one by using the חרש's money for his benefit.

steps.title: No אשם תלוי for the wife of a deaf man
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that one who sins with the wife of a חרש does not bring an אשם תלוי. Her marriage is not counted even as a doubtful marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אשי said in the name of שמואל: for the wife of a deaf man, one is not obligated to bring an אשם תלוי on her account.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: a ruling of שמואל about the marriage of a חרש and the קרבן for sinning with his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם תלוי is brought when one is not sure whether he did a sin that needs a חטאת. שמואל says sinning with the wife of a חרש does not require even this. At first glance this seems to mean her marriage is not even a doubtful marriage, but steps 21–25 will explain the ruling differently.

keyTerms.meaning: The wife of a deaf-mute
A 'suspended' guilt-offering, brought when unsure whether a sin needing a חטאת was done
Obligated

steps.confusionAlert: Do not decide yet why שמואל exempts him. The first idea is that a חרש's marriage is not even a doubt. In the end (step 25), the גמרא explains that the marriage is a doubt, and the real reason is that an אשם תלוי needs the case of 'one piece out of two'.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Chiyya bar Ashi said that Shmuel said:
The wife of a deaf-mute —
one is not obligated for her in a guilt-offering for uncertainty.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching about the status of a חרש's marriage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Relations with the wife of a חרש do not require even an אשם תלוי.

steps.title: A possible support from the משנה about תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that a משנה supports שמואל. A חרש's תרומה is simply not תרומה, so his actions have no Torah effect at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say a משנה supports him? Five people should not separate תרומה, and if they did, their תרומה is not תרומה. They are: a חרש, a שוטה, a קטן, one who separates תרומה from produce that isn't his, and a גוי who separated a Jew's produce, even with the Jew's permission. His תרומה is not תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible proof for שמואל from a משנה. The word 'לימא' tells us the proof is only a suggestion and may be tested next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a חרש's תרומה is 'not תרומה.' It does not call it doubtful תרומה. If a חרש's actions have no effect at all, his marriage should also not be even a doubtful marriage. That fits שמואל's ruling of no אשם תלוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say it supports him?
Separate תרומה
The portion of produce given to a כהן
A person who is not mentally competent
With permission

phrases.english: Shall we say this supports him:
Five may not separate teruma,
and if they separated —
their teruma is not teruma.
And these are they:
a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor,
and one who separates from what is not his,
and a gentile who separated a Jew's produce
even with the Jew's permission —
his teruma is not teruma.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a source supporting שמואל's ruling in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that a חרש's marriage is not even doubtful, so there is no אשם תלוי
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה תרומות 1:1: a חרש's תרומה is not תרומה at all, which shows his actions have no Torah effect.

steps.title: שמואל follows רבי אלעזר, who treats a חרש's תרומה as doubtful
steps.stepSummary: The proof for שמואל is pushed away. שמואל follows רבי אלעזר, who says a חרש's תרומה is a doubt, not simply nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: No proof: שמואל holds like רבי אלעזר. A ברייתא teaches that רבי יצחק said in the name of רבי אלעזר: the תרומה of a חרש does not go back to ordinary status, because it is a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof it brought for שמואל in the last step. It says שמואל actually follows a different view, the view of רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 20 the גמרא thought the משנה showed that a חרש's actions mean nothing at all. Now it quotes רבי אלעזר, who says a חרש's תרומה is a ספק, so it can't just be eaten as חולין. This sets up a problem: if a חרש's action is a doubt, his marriage should be a doubt too.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן; non-כהנים may not eat it
Ordinary food that anyone may eat
A doubt; something whose status is uncertain
'It is taught', which introduces a ברייתא

phrases.english: He said it in accordance with Rabbi Elazar.
As it is taught: Rabbi Yitzchak says
in the name of Rabbi Elazar:
The terumah of a deaf-mute does not go out to ordinary status,
because it is a doubt.
phrases.notes: We aren't sure whether a חרש's separating counts, so we treat the food both ways and don't let it be eaten as ordinary food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the משנה offered in step 20
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The support for שמואל from the משנה about a חרש's תרומה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שמואל does not follow that משנה. He follows רבי אלעזר, who treats a חרש's act as a doubt.

steps.title: Then the man should bring a guilt-offering for uncertainty
steps.stepSummary: If שמואל holds a חרש's acts are a doubt, the חרש's marriage is a doubt too. So the sinner should bring an אשם תלוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: If שמואל holds like רבי אלעזר, then the man who sins with a חרש's wife should also have to bring an אשם תלוי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל. Following רבי אלעזר seems to lead to the opposite of what שמואל ruled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם תלוי is brought when a person may have done a sin that would require a חטאת. If the חרש's marriage is a doubtful marriage, sinning with his wife is a possible sin of אשת איש. That should require an אשם תלוי, yet שמואל said it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: A guilt-offering brought when one is unsure whether he did a sin that would require a חטאת
He holds, meaning this is his opinion
Let him be obligated

phrases.english: If he holds like Rabbi Elazar,
he should also be obligated in a guilt-offering for uncertainty!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי סְבִירָא כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, אָשָׁם תָּלוּי נָמֵי לִיחַיַּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim in step 21 that שמואל follows רבי אלעזר
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that there is no אשם תלוי (step 19)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a חרש's acts are a doubt, his marriage is a doubtful marriage, and a doubtful sin normally requires an אשם תלוי.

steps.title: A guilt-offering for uncertainty needs the case of one piece out of two
steps.stepSummary: An אשם תלוי is brought only when the doubt is which of two items was eaten, one forbidden and one permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: We need the case of one piece out of two pieces.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that an אשם תלוי is not brought for every doubt. It applies only to a specific kind of doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The classic case is two pieces of fat, one forbidden and one permitted, where the person doesn't know which he ate. Here there is only one woman, and the doubt is about her own status. That is not the 'two pieces' kind of doubt, so no אשם תלוי.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One piece out of two pieces': the case where one of two items is forbidden and the person doesn't know which he ate
We require

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל is not saying the חרש's marriage is certainly invalid. It may still be a doubt. He is only saying this type of doubt doesn't bring an אשם תלוי.

phrases.english: We require one piece out of two pieces.
phrases.notes: Picture two pieces on the table, one forbidden and one permitted. You ate one but don't know which.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing when the law of אשם תלוי applies
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any doubtful sin requires an אשם תלוי
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a doubt of 'one piece out of two' requires it, and the חרש's wife is a single-item doubt

steps.title: רבי אלעזר requires a guilt-offering even for a כוי
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר himself rules that one who eats the fat of a כוי brings an אשם תלוי, even though there is only one item.
steps.simpleTranslation: But does רבי אלעזר require 'one piece out of two'? A ברייתא teaches that רבי אלעזר says: for a כוי, one must bring an אשם תלוי for eating its fat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 23. רבי אלעזר does not seem to require the 'two pieces' case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כוי is an animal we are unsure about: is it a domestic animal, whose fat is forbidden, or a wild one, whose fat is allowed? There is only one piece of fat, and the doubt is about the animal's status. Still, רבי אלעזר requires an אשם תלוי, so how can שמואל follow him?

keyTerms.meaning: A kosher animal whose status is in doubt: is it domestic or wild?
Forbidden fat of a domestic animal
'But it is taught': it introduces a ברייתא that contradicts

phrases.english: But does Rabbi Elazar require
one piece out of two pieces?
But it is taught: Rabbi Elazar says:

phrases.aramaic: כּוֹי — חַיָּיבִין עַל חֶלְבּוֹ אָשָׁם תָּלוּי.
phrases.english: A koy — one is obligated for its fat to bring a guilt-offering for uncertainty.
phrases.notes: The fat of a wild animal is allowed and the fat of a domestic animal is forbidden. A כוי could be either.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי בָּעֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר חֲתִיכָה מִשְׁתֵּי חֲתִיכוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 23 using רבי אלעזר's own ruling
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שמואל, following רבי אלעזר, requires 'one piece out of two'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעזר requires an אשם תלוי for the single-item doubt of a כוי, so he does not require two pieces

steps.title: שמואל agrees with רבי אלעזר on one point and disagrees on another
steps.stepSummary: שמואל follows רבי אלעזר that a חרש's acts are a doubt. He disagrees with him about when an אשם תלוי is brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל holds like רבי אלעזר in one matter and disagrees with him in another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שמואל does not follow רבי אלעזר on everything. He takes one of his views and rejects the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל agrees with רבי אלעזר that a חרש's actions are a doubt. On אשם תלוי, though, he holds it needs 'one piece out of two', against רבי אלעזר's ruling about the כוי. So the חרש's wife is a doubtful marriage, but sinning with her brings no אשם תלוי.

keyTerms.meaning: In one matter
He disagrees with him

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's ruling has two parts. (1) Like רבי אלעזר, a חרש's actions are a doubt. (2) Against רבי אלעזר, an אשם תלוי is only for 'one piece out of two pieces.' Together these explain why sinning with a חרש's wife brings no אשם תלוי.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that an אמורא can follow a תנא on one issue and still disagree with him on a separate issue.

phrases.english: Shmuel holds like Rabbi Elazar in one matter,
and disagrees with him in one matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמוּאֵל סָבַר כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּחֲדָא, וּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the views: partial agreement with רבי אלעזר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If שמואל follows רבי אלעזר, he must follow him on אשם תלוי too
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל follows him only on the status of a חרש and disagrees about the אשם תלוי

steps.title: Another version: שמואל requires an אשם תלוי for the wife of a deaf-mute
steps.stepSummary: In a second version, רב חייא בר אשי quotes שמואל: someone who sins with the wife of a חרש is obligated to bring an אשם תלוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say the teaching went differently. רב חייא בר אשי said in the name of שמואל: if a man has relations with the wife of a חרש, he must bring an אשם תלוי (a guilt-offering for a doubtful sin).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of שמואל's statement. Here שמואל clearly says the sinner brings an אשם תלוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier version, the question of an אשם תלוי came up only as a challenge against שמואל. Here it is שמואל's own ruling. This treats the חרש's marriage as a doubtful marriage, so relations with his wife are a doubtful sin.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say; it introduces a second version of a teaching
The wife of a deaf-mute, who married her through his own act
A guilt-offering brought when a person is not sure whether he sinned
One is obligated on her account

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. It is the same teaching of שמואל told a second way, so do not mix up the two versions.

phrases.english: And there are those who say:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Chiyya bar Ashi said that Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵשֶׁת חֵרֵשׁ חַיָּיבִין עָלֶיהָ אָשָׁם תָּלוּי.
phrases.english: For the wife of a deaf-mute, one is obligated to bring a guilt-offering for uncertainty.
phrases.notes: He means a man who had relations with her by mistake. Since her marriage is only a maybe, his sin is only a maybe.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This gives a second version of the whole שמואל discussion. Here the אשם תלוי is part of שמואל's ruling instead of a challenge against him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Relations with the wife of a חרש require an אשם תלוי, because his marriage is a doubt.

steps.title: Challenge from the rule that five people may not separate תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects using the משנה that five kinds of people, including a חרש, may not separate תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא challenges this. We learned that five kinds of people may not separate תרומה, and a חרש is one of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's ruling. A משנה seems to say that a חרש's actions do nothing at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a חרש's תרומה is not תרומה at all, then his acts have no legal effect. His marriage would then be nothing, not even a doubt, and there would be no reason for an אשם תלוי.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection; a challenge from an authoritative source
Five may not separate תרומה; a משנה listing people whose תרומה does not work
The portion of produce given to a כהן

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Five may not separate teruma!
phrases.notes: This is the start of a משנה in תרומות. The חרש is on that list of five.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This challenges the ruling of step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that the wife of a חרש brings an אשם תלוי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה suggests a חרש's acts have no effect at all. So his marriage is nothing, not a doubt, and no אשם תלוי should be needed.

steps.title: שמואל follows רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that שמואל holds like רבי אלעזר, who says a חרש's תרומה is a doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל holds like רבי אלעזר, who says a חרש's תרומה is a doubt, not nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. שמואל follows רבי אלעזר, who disagrees with the plain reading of that משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אלעזר, a חרש's acts are a doubt. So the marriage is a doubt, and an אשם תלוי fits. In this version there is no second problem about one item, because רבי אלעזר himself requires an אשם תלוי even for a single item.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like; he agrees with that opinion
The תנא who says a חרש's תרומה is a doubt

steps.whatToRemember: In this version, שמואל follows רבי אלעזר on both points: a חרש's acts are a doubt, and that doubt is enough for an אשם תלוי.

phrases.english: He holds in accordance with Rabbi Elazar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the challenge of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Places the ruling within a תנא's opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone holds that a חרש's acts are nothing, so there is no doubtful sin.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל follows רבי אלעזר, for whom a חרש's acts are a doubt, so an אשם תלוי applies.

steps.title: רב אשי asks for רבי אלעזר's reason
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks why רבי אלעזר treats a חרש's actions as a doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי asked: what is רבי אלעזר's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רב אשי wants to understand why רבי אלעזר is unsure about a חרש. This sets up the possibilities that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר says a חרש's acts are a doubt, but he does not explain what the doubt is about. רב אשי is about to offer possible explanations.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked; it usually introduces a question with two possible answers
What is the reason?

phrases.english: Rav Ashi raised a dilemma:
What is the reason of Rabbi Elazar?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא רַב אָשֵׁי: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After establishing that שמואל follows רבי אלעזר, the גמרא now asks why רבי אלעזר holds this way.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly is רבי אלעזר unsure about regarding a חרש?

steps.title: First possibility: a weak mind that may still be clear
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי offers a first possibility. רבי אלעזר is sure that a חרש's mind is weak, but unsure whether it is still clear.
steps.simpleTranslation: One possibility: רבי אלעזר is sure that a חרש has a weak mind. But he is unsure whether that mind is still clear...
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי lays out the first side of his question. The sentence continues on the next amud, where the other side comes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the doubt is not whether a חרש has any understanding at all. It is whether his weaker understanding is still clear enough to count. A mind can be weak in general but clear about simple things he does.

keyTerms.meaning: A weak mind; limited understanding
A clear mind; understanding what he is doing
He is in doubt about it

steps.confusionAlert: "Weak" and "clear" are not opposites here. A mind can be weak overall and still clear about what he is doing.

phrases.english: It is obvious to him
that a deaf-mute has a weak mind,
